entries.title: Ask for Help Without Sounding Helpless
entries.hook: A strong request for help has three parts. Use this formula.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I’m trying to send the client update before three.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: I’m stuck on choosing the two results for the opening. Could you mark the two you would lead with?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Goal, exact obstacle, smallest useful help. That sounds responsible, not helpless.

entries.answer: The goal, the exact obstacle, and the smallest useful help.
entries.visualBrief: Bright illustrated shared workspace with an adult woman and adult man beside a three-point notebook, shoulders-up, all hands hidden below desk, rust, navy and cream palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Workplace Idiom: Get the Ball Rolling
entries.hook: Your manager says, ‘Let’s get the ball rolling.’ What should you do?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The team has approved the idea. Maya says, ‘I’ll book the first meeting so we can get the ball rolling.’

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: She is not looking for a ball. Get the ball rolling means start a process or activity.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: In other words, move from discussion to the first concrete action, even if the project is still small.

entries.prompt: Does it mean start, delay, or cancel?
entries.visualBrief: Bright illustrated modern office with one confident adult professional beside a simple project board made of abstract shapes, upper body only, hands out of frame, teal and amber palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Workplace Idiom: Keep Me in the Loop
entries.hook: If a colleague says, ‘Keep me in the loop,’ what do they want?

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Please keep me in the loop, especially if the delivery date changes.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: Of course. I’ll send you every important update.

turns.speaker: leo
turns.text: Keep someone in the loop means keep them informed and involved.

turns.speaker: mia
turns.text: So you need the decisions and changes that affect your work, not every tiny detail.

entries.answer: Important updates about the supplier and delivery date.
entries.visualBrief: Polished illustrated office conversation between two adult colleagues with a clean abstract update board behind them, chest-up, all hands hidden, blue-green and warm cream palette, no readable text.

entries.title: A Clear Way to Say No When Someone Asks for Help
entries.hook: You cannot help with everything, but you can answer without sounding cold.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: A colleague asked, ‘Can you review my whole report today?’

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The answer was clear: ‘I cannot review the whole report today, but I can look at the opening paragraph after lunch.’

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: That answer works because it names a firm limit and offers a smaller useful action. Only offer the smaller action if you truly have capacity.

entries.prompt: What two things make the answer clear?
entries.answer: A firm limit and a smaller possible action.
entries.visualBrief: Warm illustrated shared office with two adult colleagues having a respectful conversation across a desk, shoulders-up, hands fully out of frame, rust, navy and cream palette, no readable text.
